It watches for gold-target cells, mine candidates and reported workings, clearing since 2020 and long fronts along roads and rivers.
properties.first_season: Confirm reporting lines with county and traditional authorities in Wau and map gold-target cells and mine candidates in the Kuajok community zone bounded by Wau-Gogrial Road and Wau-Aweil Road. Prepare for herd arrivals on the corridor in September and October along Wau - Raja road and tertiary road.
properties.short: Focal point based in Wau covers community and corridor zones around Kuajok and Wau, linking authorities with mining and herd monitoring year-round.

properties.brief: The focal point is based year-round in Maridi, a town of 50,584 people where county and traditional authorities are seated, covering two nearby team sites within 120 km including Maridi and Makpandu* (nearest_place, unverified). It serves zone 267, about 1.2 million ha in South Sudan with an estimated population of 3,345, bounded on the east northeast by the Juba-Rumbek-Bentiu Highway road for 72 km, on the west southwest by Nahr al Jur for 58 km, and on the southwest southeast by the Maridi-Yambio Highway road for 36 km. Transhumant herders using the corridor move through in onset months 10 and 11, with bundles arriving from the northeast and west. The team watches for artisanal activity across nine gold-target cells, one candidate and two watchlist sites, long fronts totalling about 3,256 km, and low clearing since 2020 of about 1 km² with no reported workings.
properties.first_season: First, meet county and traditional authorities in Maridi to confirm reporting lines for the two unheld sites within 120 km. Second, verify the 64 km boundary along the geological contact that is not visible on the ground and needs beacons, working with herders arriving in month 10.
properties.short: Based in Maridi, the one-person focal point monitors a 1.2 million ha corridor west of Maridi for transhumance movements and artisanal pressure.
